newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares drift lower early on rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares drift lower early on rate fears.

text.p: Singapore shares drifted lower on Friday morning due to continuing technical pressure and fears over a potential U.S. interest rate hike, dealers said.
Institutional investors led selling on blue chips and index-linked counters, while retail buyers were mostly subdued.
"People are resisting doing too much before clearer direction on U.S. interest rates," a foreign brokerage dealer said.
The market was seen trading narrowly between 1,950 and 2,050 with higher interest rates likely to push it lower.
At 2035 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) fell 11.57 points to 2,008.60, veering towards critical 2,000 support.
The foreign tranches of OCBC bank and DBS bank suffered a loss of Singapore 10 cents to S$16.90 each.
Some banks and property companies with exposure to Thailand and mortgage lending rates could be vulnerable to more selling in the near-term, dealers said.
Meanwhile, issues like Cycle & Carriage shed 10 cents to S$14.30 and Fraser & Neave also lost 10 cents to S$10.40.
Singapore Telecom shares eased another two cents from its previous close to S$2.52, with news of pricing cuts on mobile phones amid stiffening competition, adding pressure.
